name: JavaScript & runtime
description: Async code that works until it doesn't: how the runtime really schedules, scopes and copies things.

concepts.name: Event loop
concepts.description: The call stack runs to completion; then microtasks (promise callbacks) drain before the next macrotask (timers, I/O).

concepts.name: Promises
concepts.description: A promise is a placeholder for a future value; then/catch callbacks run as microtasks and chains pass values along.

concepts.name: async/await
concepts.description: await pauses only the async function, not the thread; every async function returns a promise.

concepts.name: Closures
concepts.description: A function keeps access to the variables of the scope where it was created, even after that scope has returned.

concepts.name: this binding
concepts.description: this is decided by how a function is called, not where it is written; arrow functions take this from the enclosing scope.

concepts.name: == vs ===
concepts.description: === compares without type conversion; == converts types first, which produces surprising results.

concepts.name: Mutation vs copy
concepts.description: Objects and arrays are passed by reference; spreading copies only one level deep.

concepts.name: Hoisting
concepts.description: var and function declarations are hoisted; let and const are hoisted too but unusable before their line (temporal dead zone).

concepts.name: var, let and const
concepts.description: var is function-scoped, let and const are block-scoped; const forbids reassignment, not mutation.

concepts.name: Array methods
concepts.description: map, filter and reduce return new values; sort and splice mutate in place, and sort compares strings by default.

concepts.name: Types and coercion
concepts.description: typeof, truthy and falsy values, and the implicit conversions JavaScript performs with + and comparisons.

concepts.name: Error handling
concepts.description: try/catch only catches what is thrown synchronously or awaited; an unawaited rejected promise escapes it.

name: Frontend
description: Components that render forty times: the browser and framework mechanics behind a UI.

concepts.name: DOM and reflow
concepts.description: Reading layout after writing styles forces the browser to recalculate layout synchronously.

concepts.name: State and re-render
concepts.description: A component re-renders when its state or props change; derived values should be computed, not stored.

concepts.name: Flexbox and grid
concepts.description: Flexbox lays out one dimension, grid two; both replace float and table layout hacks.

concepts.name: CSS specificity
concepts.description: IDs beat classes, classes beat elements; later rules win ties, and !important overrides the normal order.

concepts.name: Accessibility
concepts.description: Semantic elements, labels and keyboard focus make an interface usable with assistive technology.

concepts.name: Memo and lazy loading
concepts.description: Memoization skips repeated work; lazy loading defers code until it is needed.

name: Backend, APIs & architecture
description: Endpoints without validation and layers without purpose: how a server should behave.

concepts.name: HTTP semantics and status codes
concepts.description: Methods carry meaning (safe, idempotent) and status codes tell the client what happened.

concepts.name: REST design
concepts.description: Resources are nouns in URLs; the method says what to do with them.

concepts.name: Validation
concepts.description: Validate every input at the boundary and reject it with a clear 400 before any work happens.

concepts.name: Error handling
concepts.description: Return consistent error bodies and never leak stack traces or internal messages to clients.

concepts.name: Authentication flow
concepts.description: Authentication proves who you are; authorization decides what you may do.

concepts.name: Middleware
concepts.description: Middleware runs in order around every request; its position in the pipeline matters.

concepts.name: Coupling
concepts.description: Modules that know too much about each other change together; dependencies should point inward.

name: Databases & SQL
description: The query that works on a hundred rows and dies on a million.

concepts.name: JOIN types
concepts.description: INNER JOIN keeps matching rows only; LEFT JOIN keeps every left row and fills missing right columns with NULL.

concepts.name: Indexes
concepts.description: An index turns a full table scan into a lookup, at the cost of slower writes and extra storage.

concepts.name: N+1 queries
concepts.description: Loading a list and then querying once per item sends N+1 queries where one join or batch would do.

concepts.name: Transactions and ACID
concepts.description: A transaction makes several statements succeed or fail together.

concepts.name: Normalization
concepts.description: Store each fact once; duplicated data drifts apart when only one copy is updated.

concepts.name: NULL semantics
concepts.description: NULL means unknown: comparisons with NULL are neither true nor false, so use IS NULL.

concepts.name: GROUP BY and HAVING
concepts.description: GROUP BY collapses rows into groups; WHERE filters rows before grouping, HAVING filters groups after.

concepts.name: Subqueries
concepts.description: A subquery can produce a value, a list for IN, or a table; EXISTS stops at the first match.

concepts.name: Keys and constraints
concepts.description: Primary keys, foreign keys, UNIQUE and CHECK let the database reject bad data itself.

concepts.name: Isolation and locking
concepts.description: Concurrent transactions can see each other's changes depending on the isolation level; locks prevent lost updates.

concepts.name: Logical query order
concepts.description: SQL runs FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT, ORDER BY, LIMIT, in that order, not as written.

concepts.name: Views
concepts.description: A view is a stored query used like a table; it holds no data unless it is materialized.

name: Networking & web protocols
description: The CORS error that goes straight into ChatGPT: what happens between browser and server.

concepts.name: TCP vs UDP
concepts.description: TCP delivers ordered, reliable streams; UDP sends independent packets with no delivery guarantee.

concepts.name: DNS
concepts.description: DNS translates names into IP addresses through a chain of cached lookups.

concepts.name: HTTP methods, caching and cookies
concepts.description: Cache headers decide who may reuse a response and for how long; cookies travel with every matching request.

concepts.name: CORS
concepts.description: The browser blocks reading cross-origin responses unless the server allows the origin.

concepts.name: TLS
concepts.description: TLS encrypts the connection and proves the server's identity with a certificate.

concepts.name: WebSocket vs HTTP
concepts.description: WebSocket keeps one connection open for messages in both directions; HTTP is request and response.

name: Cybersecurity
description: AI writes vulnerable code and nobody reads it: the mistakes attackers look for first.

concepts.name: SQL injection
concepts.description: Concatenating input into SQL lets it become code; parameters keep data as data.

concepts.name: XSS
concepts.description: Inserting untrusted text into HTML without escaping lets it run as script in other users' browsers.

concepts.name: CSRF
concepts.description: A forged request from another site rides on the victim's cookies unless the server checks its origin.

concepts.name: Hashing vs encryption
concepts.description: Encryption is reversible with a key; password hashing is one-way and deliberately slow.

concepts.name: Secrets in code
concepts.description: Keys committed to a repository are public forever; load them from the environment.

concepts.name: JWT pitfalls
concepts.description: A JWT is signed, not encrypted; the server must verify the signature, algorithm and expiry.

concepts.name: Input validation
concepts.description: Validate on the server with allow-lists; client-side checks are a convenience, not protection.

name: Algorithms & data structures
description: It works, but it's O(n²): choosing the structure that keeps code fast.

concepts.name: Complexity
concepts.description: Big O describes how work grows with input size; nested loops over the same data are usually O(n²).

concepts.name: Hash map vs list
concepts.description: A hash map finds a key in constant time on average; searching a list is linear.

concepts.name: Recursion
concepts.description: A recursive function needs a base case; each call uses stack space until it returns.

concepts.name: Sorting
concepts.description: Good general sorts are O(n log n); a stable sort keeps the order of equal elements.

concepts.name: BFS and DFS
concepts.description: Breadth-first search explores level by level with a queue; depth-first goes deep with a stack.

concepts.name: Stack and queue
concepts.description: A stack is last in, first out; a queue is first in, first out.

name: How AI works
description: Used every day, rarely understood: how language models work and when they are wrong.

concepts.name: Tokens
concepts.description: Models read and write tokens, pieces of words; limits and prices are counted in tokens, not characters.

concepts.name: Context window
concepts.description: The model sees only what is in the current request, up to a fixed number of tokens.

concepts.name: Hallucinations
concepts.description: A model produces likely-sounding text, so it can state wrong facts and invent sources with full confidence.

concepts.name: Temperature and sampling
concepts.description: Sampling picks the next token from a probability distribution; temperature makes the choice more or less random.

concepts.name: Embeddings
concepts.description: An embedding is a vector that places similar meanings close together, so similarity becomes distance.

concepts.name: Retrieval-augmented generation
concepts.description: RAG retrieves relevant documents and puts them into the prompt so answers are grounded in them.

concepts.name: Prompt structure
concepts.description: Instructions, context and examples in clear sections; the system prompt sets the rules for the conversation.

concepts.name: Prompting vs fine-tuning
concepts.description: Fine-tuning changes the model's weights with examples; prompting changes only the input.

concepts.name: When not to trust it
concepts.description: Check generated code, numbers and citations; the model has no built-in way to know it is wrong.

concepts.name: Structured output
concepts.description: Asking for JSON is not a guarantee; validate and parse the output, or use a schema-constrained mode.

concepts.name: Calling an LLM API
concepts.description: The API is stateless: you resend the conversation each call and set limits such as max_tokens yourself.

concepts.name: Training vs inference
concepts.description: Knowledge comes from training data up to a cutoff; at inference the model only predicts, it does not learn.
